name: jev-sidecar-go
description: Go port of jev-gate (the Jev pre-flight gate: agent hooks, decide/outcome/precision and the sidecar `serve` with POST /decide/<use>, POST /outcome/<use>, GET /health, GET /precision), shadow stage: runs next to the Python jev-sidecar on its own port with no key, outcome journal and budget of its own, outside every request path (ticket #1879)

native_build._doc: Same multi-stage template as c3bot-relay-go (#1873): compiled in golang on the arch-matched runner (oci-apps is arm64), shipped as one static binary on distroless static nonroot.

api.description: Same contract as jev-sidecar: POST /decide/<use>, POST /outcome/<use>, GET /health, GET /precision.

parity-compare._doc: Reference = _shared/jev-gate/jev_gate.py (python3). Every scenario (claude/goose hooks incl. the never-auto-approve list, redaction, budget, impact and route_context against a mock code-graph MCP, goose-prompt, decide/outcome/precision, the sidecar HTTP surface) runs through both with the same stdin, environment, mock Decisions server and mock MCP server; stdout, the journal lines (key order included), the requests the mocks saw, the ledger, the caches and the goose context file must be identical.

parity-mutation.cmd: o=$(mktemp); PARITY_MUTATE=1 PARITY_REQUIRE=1 go test -count=1 -timeout 9m -tags parity -run 'TestParity$' ./parity/ >"$o" 2>&1; grep -q 'scenarios differ' "$o"
parity-mutation._doc: Mutation proof: the mock Decisions server skews its noul answers for the Go run only; the harness must report differing scenarios (the grep passes only then, not on a build error).

_doc_shadow: Shadow stage (#1879). The live Python jev-sidecar (port 3110, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, volume jev-sidecar-data) and every in-image jev-gate (claude, goose, hermes) are untouched; hermes keeps the Python module as its plugin shim (select_tools and route_context stay in jev_gate.py). The config is embedded in the binary (a unit test keeps it identical to _shared/jev-gate/jev-gate.json). Known dialect notes: \\s and \\S follow Python's Unicode whitespace; \\b and \\w stay ASCII (a non-ASCII letter before a secret prefix counts as a boundary, so Go redacts slightly more, never less).
